subject: POC kickoff & hands-on prompt lab — calendar coordination and prework
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@blueleaf.ai>
Cc: Tom Wallace <tom.w@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff windows + hands-on prompt lab (agenda + prework)

Hi Sana / Tom —

Excited to get the BlueLeaf POC started. To keep things tight and make the most of the hands-on prompt lab we propose a 2.5 hour kickoff + workshop block that covers:

- 30m: kickoff + goals alignment
- 60m: prompt inventory review and structured output requirements
- 30m: routing & latency expectations + KV/prefix caching discussion
- 30m: load-test plan and canary run (optional short live run)

Suggested windows (all PDT):
- Tue Apr 27, 9:00–11:30
- Wed Apr 28, 13:00–15:30
- Thu Apr 29, 8:00–10:30

Prework for BlueLeaf: please complete the attached prompt-inventory-template.csv with 6–12 representative prompts (happy path and failure examples) and flag which prompts need structured outputs (JSON schema) or external tool calls. Also attach any SLOs you want us to hit for the load test (p50/p95 latencies, target concurrency).

Attachments: redwood-poc-agenda.pdf, prompt-inventory-template.csv, sow-draft-blueleaf-v1.docx

If you confirm a preferred window I will loop in Ben (ops) and Karthik (runtime) for the technical runbook. If none of these work, send a few alternative slots and we’ll rebalance.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff windows + hands-on prompt lab (agenda + prework)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear agenda. Wed Apr 28, 13:00–15:30 PDT works best for our team.

A couple of quick clarifications before we lock:
- For the load test, can you share the expected concurrency profile and whether the canary run will use production traffic or synthetic traffic?
- For structured outputs: we have two critical prompts that must return strict JSON schemas for downstream processing — we will flag them in the inventory.
- Procurement may need a short SOW update (Tom, looping you).

We’ll aim to have the prompt inventory completed by EOD Tue Apr 27.

Cheers,
Sana
Head of AI Integrations, BlueLeaf
Sana.Patel@blueleaf.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Tom Wallace <tom.w@blueleaf.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff windows + hands-on prompt lab (agenda + prework)

Perfect — Wed Apr 28 13:00–15:30 PDT is confirmed tentatively. I’ve attached the prompt-inventory-template again and an updated agenda with minute-level timings.

Answers to your clarifying questions:
- Load test concurrency: for the workshop we recommend a stepped synthetic profile: 1) 5 concurrent users (warmup), 2) 20 concurrent for 5 minutes, 3) 50 concurrent peak for 3 minutes (this is to validate batching and autoscale behavior). We will not use production traffic for the canary — we’ll synthesize payloads from your inventory examples. See loadtest-profile.yaml attached.
- Canary plan: short live canary only if you opt in during the session; by default we run a local synthetic run to validate routing/caching.

Ben will lead the load/test orchestration and Karthik will own runtime settings and quantization/config suggestions during the session. They may ask for a short pre-call with your infra team if you want private deployment routing tested.

Tom — if procurement needs an updated SOW, I can share a pared-down SOW that covers the workshop goals and acceptance criteria.

Next steps:
1) Sana: confirm final attendee list + attach the inventory by EOD Tue Apr 27.
2) Ben/Karthik: prep runbook and quick run-through on Tue afternoon.
3) Marissa: send calendar invite + drive folder link once attendees confirmed.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Hi team — quick ops note ahead of Wed’s session.

Load-test plan (summary):
- Tool: locust + synthetic clients (we’ll provide the dockerized runner)
- Profiles: see attached loadtest-profile.yaml for ramp schedule and payload templates
- Metrics we’ll surface: qps, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token/sec, batching statistics, cache hit ratio
- Safety: the canary will run in a sandboxed cluster, not against prod endpoints. If BlueLeaf wants us to exercise routing policies (region failover, model fallback) let us know and we’ll stage that in the runbook.

Pre-call ask for BlueLeaf infra (optional, 30m): Wed Apr 28 10:00–10:30 PDT — we’ll confirm networking/egress and any VPC peering needed.

Attachments: loadtest-profile.yaml

If procurement needs the SOW snippet for scope/acceptance, I can generate that and cc Marissa.
